summary: The run developed reasonable damage and scaling through Inflame, Limit Break+, Shuriken, and several strong attacks, but it accumulated severe HP losses in hallway combats. Defensive and survival resources were not prioritized enough relative to additional scaling, and the Guardian fight reached a critical 2 HP state where small offensive choices became dangerous. The run ultimately lost with the Guardian at 15/240 HP.

lessons.title: Prioritize immediate defense over more scaling when survival is already strained
lessons.situation: When HP has been falling across combats and a reward offers both a defensive card and another scaling or damage card.
lessons.lesson: Prefer cards that immediately improve block, draw, or hand quality over additional scaling unless the deck is already surviving reliably. In particular, do not automatically choose Limit Break-type scaling when a defensive option such as Shrug It Off is available.
evidence_points: At Floor 11, the reward offered Shrug It Off and Limit Break; Limit Break was chosen.
The final deck contained Inflame and upgraded Limit Break, but only four Defends plus Shrug It Off, True Grit, Intimidate, and Warcry as clear defensive or defensive-support cards.
The Guardian fight later reached HP 21 on Turn 12 and HP 2 on Turn 14.
lessons.reasoning: The run already had multiple ways to increase damage, while its HP trajectory and final combat show that surviving incoming attacks was the limiting problem. This makes the defensive reward the more robust choice in similar situations.

lessons.title: At critical HP, do not spend surplus block energy on marginal damage
lessons.situation: When at very low HP against an enemy showing an attack intent and the current block is not clearly sufficient.
lessons.lesson: Calculate whether the current block safely covers the attack before attacking. If it does not, use the available Defend effects instead of converting the remaining energy into a Strike or other low-impact attack.
evidence_points: On Turn 15 at HP 2 with The Guardian showing ATTACK, after playing Shrug It Off the agent had 8 Block and 2 Energy, then chose Defend followed by Strike.
At that exact decision, both Defend and Strike were legal alternatives.
On Turn 16, the agent was still at HP 2 with 0 Block and again faced an ATTACK intent.
lessons.reasoning: The Turn 15 Strike provided limited progress while leaving only 13 Block before an attack at 2 HP. Because the exact incoming damage is unavailable, the claim is conditional rather than certain, but at this survival threshold the safer default is to add block unless coverage is already established.

lessons.title: Evaluate the final campfire for boss survivability, not only damage scaling
lessons.situation: At the last campfire before an Act boss, especially after hallway fights have caused substantial HP loss.
lessons.lesson: Before upgrading an offensive scaling card, compare it against the value of healing or upgrading a defensive option. If the boss plan depends on surviving several attack turns, entering with more HP or stronger defense can be worth more than increasing an already adequate damage engine.
evidence_points: At Floor 15, immediately before the Guardian, the agent had 68/80 HP and chose smith, upgrading Limit Break.
The Guardian combat then reduced the player to 21 HP by Turn 12 and 2 HP by Turn 14.
The run ended with The Guardian still at 15/240 HP.
lessons.reasoning: The final upgrade improved scaling, but the boss fight was decided by survival margins rather than lack of access to damage. The repeated drop to critical HP indicates that the final campfire decision should have explicitly prioritized boss endurance.
